models.name: F1 Xtreme
models.tagline: The sharpest hull we build, offered in race trim and in leisure trim.
models.intro: The F1 Xtreme is the point of the range. A deep-V racing hull built entirely in composite, set up for competition and then re-trimmed, seat by seat, for owners who want that hull on a Sunday. Nothing about the running surface changes between the two — only what sits on top of it.

features.p: The hull is the constant. A fine entry and a hard-run aft section that stays planted through chop at speed, without the slamming that usually comes with that much deadrise.
Race trim strips weight and adds restraint systems. Leisure trim adds upholstered seating, storage and finish. The performance you feel underneath is the same.
Hull, deck and structure are laid up in composite at Willebroek. No wood, no bonded steel — a stiffer platform that keeps its shape season after season.

models.name: F2 Xtreme
models.tagline: The same discipline as the F1, in a hull built to be driven more often.
models.intro: The F2 Xtreme takes the Xtreme running surface and gives it a little more forgiveness. It races, and it also does the thing an F1 will not — long days, more people, less ceremony. For most owners this is the one that gets used.

features.p: Trimmed to stay comfortable across a wider band of speed and sea state, rather than being sharpest at one narrow point of it.
In leisure trim the cockpit is arranged around movement — boarding, sitting, standing at the helm — without softening the boat underneath.
The same hull is delivered in competition specification, with the seating, restraint and rigging changes that go with it.

models.name: TS Model
models.intro: The TS is a pure competition boat. There is no leisure version and no attempt at one. Every decision in it — layout, weight, rigging, where the crew sits — is made against a stopwatch.

features.t: Weight where it earns its place
features.p: Structure is put where load goes and removed everywhere else. The result is a boat that changes direction when asked rather than when persuaded.
The cockpit is built around the driver and throttleman, not fitted around a deck mould that already existed.
Rigging, trim and propeller selection are specified for the course, not delivered as a compromise that suits none of them.

models.name: FTX 27 R
models.tagline: The FTX 27, taken to the course.
models.intro: The R is what the FTX 27 becomes when the finish comes out and the rigging goes in. Same 27-foot hull, race structure, race seating, race weight. If you already know the FTX, you know how this one behaves — only sooner.

features.p: The FTX 27 running surface is proven in leisure use before it ever sees a course. The R inherits that behaviour rather than starting from a blank sheet.
Interior finish is removed and structure is added where competition loads demand it. Lighter overall, stiffer where it counts.
Crew positions, seating and restraint are specified to competition requirements.

models.name: 43 Leverage
models.tagline: The offshore race boat, and the largest hull we build.
models.intro: At 43 feet the Leverage is the biggest thing we build, and the one with the record to prove it. Raced as Bernico–New Star in UIM Class V1 by Nico Bertels and Frank Hemelaer, she took race 1 at the 2014 Grand Prix of Italy in Terracina, race 2 at the 2014 Abu Dhabi World Championship, and won the Venezia–Rimini leg of the 2015 UIM Class V1 World Championship. The leisure trim is the same hull with the finish put back on.

features.p: Raced as Bernico–New Star in UIM Class V1: race 1 at Terracina 2014, race 2 at the Abu Dhabi World Championship 2014, and the Venezia–Rimini leg of the 2015 V1 World Championship.
Forty-three feet of waterline holds a line through sea states that make shorter hulls negotiate. Less correction from the helm, less fatigue over distance.
The same hull with deck, seating and storage arranged for long days aboard, without giving away the performance the length buys you.

models.name: FTX 27
models.tagline: Pure power and perfect control, at 27 feet.
models.intro: The FTX 27 is the rigid hull most owners start with. Big enough to take weather seriously, small enough to handle on your own, and quick enough that nobody asks what else is in the range. It is also the hull behind our FTX 27 R race boat — which tells you most of what you need to know about how it runs.

features.p: The FTX is fast, but what owners describe first is how settled it stays while doing it. Predictable through turns, planted on the run.

features.t: A deck you can move on
features.p: Practical flow from boarding to helm to aft, with storage where you actually reach for it rather than where it was easiest to mould.
The same hull runs in competition as the FTX 27 R. Nothing about the leisure version is a softer design — only a softer fit-out.

models.name: VC 35
models.tagline: Thirty-five feet, arranged for the whole day rather than the fast part of it.
models.intro: The VC 35 is the least apologetic leisure boat we build. The extra eight feet over the FTX go into space you use — seating, shade, storage, somewhere to put people who are not currently interested in going fast. It still has the hull underneath it that makes them interested again.

features.p: Eight more feet than the FTX, spent on deck area and seating rather than on numbers in a brochure.
An ergonomic helm position built for long days on the water, with the visibility and support to stay comfortable at speed.
Premium materials and tight tolerances throughout, chosen so the boat still reads well after several seasons rather than one.

models.tagline: Racing DNA in the world of RIBs.
models.intro: Crafted with Bernico's proven hull design expertise, the 7 is where innovation meets pure excitement. Whether you're cruising coastal waters or pushing performance limits, it delivers an unparalleled experience for up to seven passengers. With options for single or dual engine configurations and constructed entirely from composite materials, it represents the pinnacle of rigid inflatable boat technology.

features.p: Built for confident driving, with a deep-V hull, a central steering console and a spacious driver's seat for better control.
Supports high-performance outboard power, with a maximum setup of 2 × 500 HP for strong acceleration and genuine top-end speed.
Supportive seats, good legroom and a smooth ride — ideal for families, group travel and long journeys.

models.tagline: Half a metre more, and it changes more than you would expect.
models.intro: The 7.6 sits between the 7 and the 8, and it exists because that half metre is worth having. More tube, more deck, a little more weight to settle the ride — without moving into a size that needs a bigger berth or a bigger tow vehicle.

features.p: More waterline settles the hull through chop and adds usable deck without pushing the boat into the next size class.
Walk-around access on both sides, with the helm positioned for visibility standing or seated.
Practical deck flow and boarding from shore or sea — the details that decide whether a RIB gets used every weekend.

models.tagline: The largest of the standard RIBs.
models.intro: Eight metres is where a RIB stops being a tender and starts being the boat you take out on purpose. More deck, more range, more people — and enough hull under you to keep going when the afternoon turns.

features.p: Enough fuel and enough hull to make a long day out a decision rather than a calculation.
Seating and storage laid out for a full boat, not for a photograph of an empty one.
Built in composite throughout, so the platform stays stiff and the finish holds up to hard use.

models.name: RX10
models.tagline: Dominating the waves with raw power and precision.
models.intro: The RX10 is what happens when the RIB range stops being modest about it. Ten metres of composite hull built for open water and long, fast passages — the boat you choose when the crossing is the point, not the obstacle.

features.p: A deep-V section designed to cross rather than to pose, holding speed through the kind of sea that ends most days early.
Rigged for high-output outboards, with structure and hardware specified to take the load over distance.
Helm ergonomics, seating and layout worked out for passages measured in hours, not minutes.

models.name: RXP14
models.intro: The RXP14 is the top of the RIB range and the largest thing we build on tubes. Fourteen metres, laid out with the space and finish of a rigid boat and the sea-keeping of a RIB — which is a combination almost nothing else offers.

features.p: Fourteen metres gives you the deck area, seating and storage of a much larger rigid hull, with the forgiveness of tubes alongside it.
Luxury details throughout — the level of finish owners expect from the top of a range, not from a large workboat.
Rigged for the power the hull can carry, with the range and reserve to use it properly.
